assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the active_provisional KONOSUBA_DUKE_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (15,221 bytes) and the active_provisional KONOSUBA_DUKE_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md (8,153 bytes; one rule, DK-R01). Their direct core is the complete MAIN13 chapter 3, chapter 4, final chapter, epilogue and bonus contexts and the bounded DUST05 scenes (P298-339 as dependent retellings of MAIN13, P369-408 as a distinct Small encounter), with qualified MAIN14 C1 P7, MAIN15 P780-788 and MAIN17 U011 P84 references. The cohort evidence index, native provenance and rule inventory are not curated on this subject and were not used. The items state that no scenario input or original first response has been serialized. The items' own labels are inputs, not conclusions; the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The MAIN13 episode from Wiz's reported first approach (C3 P148-154) through the tavern encounters, the graveyard challenge, his surrender, lich conversion, purification and final pleading (Final P404-457), with the distinct DUST05 Small encounter; later material only as attributed reports (MAIN14 repelled, MAIN15 missing with his report received, MAIN17 Kazuma's retrospective description of him blasted to death). Behavior is split at the located defeat: pre-defeat treatment of interlocutors versus the post-defeat lich conversion and improvised romance, which are not projected backward. The later white-winged gatekeeper is a different figure.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: Stated goals are located (Wiz's Demon King army office through a demonstration of superior force, Final P305-308 and P361-366; magical mastery, Final P208; an interested grievance about unpaid divine service, P326), with an unreconciled conflict between his opposition to undead and joining an army that includes them, and affect regulators across the episode. DK-R01 is one conditioned rule with support, contrary evidence, rivals and a falsifier. Not B: the model says the ordering among standing, mastery, independence and survival is unknown, ordinary caution and fear of a stronger figure remain strong rivals to the rule's distinctive cause, and the lich conversion and improvised romance are deliberately not generalized. Not D: the explicit goals, the located transitions and the rule's conditions go beyond an interpretation without an operational account.

A located within-episode sequence: composure, intimidation, relaxation under apparent support, escalation when Wiz does not fight seriously (Final P240-265), caution before Vanir, surrender, lich conversion and pleading, with later outcomes kept as attributed reports. Not C: the sequence is one climax, the defeat-driven transitions are not modeled as transferable state changes, and there is no development across time. Not E: the states and their triggers are located with paragraph references and kept apart.

Recipient-dependent forms are named and located: direct self-naming and fire specialization (C3 P266), grand mastery language and contemptuous 貴様/雑魚 in challenge and threat contexts, the cautious バニル殿 and polite request (Final P341), strained repeated questions under misunderstanding, the very quiet office explanation (P305-308), and the final stop/please-wait and friends-first appeal. The items state these are short written witnesses and claim no representative frequency or heard delivery. Not B: few occasions in one episode and no line inventory. Not D: the forms are conditioned on rank, recipient and goal with locators.

Drinking alone at the tavern, accepting a drink after Dust's reversal and paying for Aqua's drinks (C3 P363-364; C4 P360/P405; DUST05 P370); their games and trivia settlement are Aqua's account. Not D: a few finite transactions in one episode, and the items state that no income, home, diet, routine or hobby hierarchy is supplied.

Treatment differs by recipient and is partly explained: intimidation of Dust after his solicitation and seating after the test cover (C3 P357-363), a knife threat when Kazuma names Wiz and reduced vigilance after apparent support (C3 P400-441), Small spared explicitly because she appears connected to Vanir (DUST05 P395-406), a polite noninterference request and retreat before Vanir (Final P341-342), no visible constraint from Darkness's noble identity, and congenial rapport with Aqua until her identity disclosure. Not B: each relation rests on one encounter, the Vanir effect is not separated from generic fear of a stronger figure, and transfer to other patrons is open. Not D: DK-R01 conditions treatment on credited standing and connection with an explicit textual explanation in the Small scene.

Duke is never focalized; the narration is Kazuma's in MAIN13 and Dust's in DUST05. Affect is inferred from located conduct: bewilderment and exasperation at the marriage reading (Final P281-308), caution before Vanir, surrender and collapse, and fear with opportunistic adjustment during the final appeal (P404-457), which the items say shows no independently exposed full interior plan. Not C: no direct access and no account of his private reasoning. Not E: the affective transitions and their triggers are located.

Escalation and retreat have located triggers: intimidation of perceived weak interferers, accusations of contempt and escalation to sacred magic when Wiz does not attack seriously, caution and retreat before Vanir while asserting that his challenge should proceed (C3 P441), surrender under near suffocation, the costly lich ritual after defeat, and an improvised appeal under imminent destruction. Not B: one escalating climax; the thresholds for costly revision and surrender are weakly identified, and the items decline a general law about sacrificing convictions when cornered. Not D: the triggers that switch threat, retreat and escalation are located.

Located value conflicts and justifications: the claimed entitlement to Wiz's office by superior force, the unpaid-wages grievance used to justify sacred magic after rebellion (testimony, not a verified contract), shared categorical hostility to demons and Eris, opposition to undead overturned by his own lich conversion, and the town threat and military report. Not C: no reported weighing between options; the single costly revision happens under defeat, and the justifications are interested. Not E: the conflicts and his stated grounds are located.

His one located play is rapport with Aqua over strange creatures and shared hostility, with games and a trivia settlement only in her account (C4 P371-405); the courtship comedy is situational and depends on others' misreadings. Not D: one rapport scene.

The items cover the complete MAIN13 chapter 3, chapter 4, final chapter, epilogue and bonus contexts with a ruby-inclusive packet, separate the dependent DUST05 retellings from the distinct Small encounter, and qualify the later MAIN14, MAIN15 and MAIN17 references. Not B: DUST05 is bounded, no exercise inputs or first responses are serialized, and the items do not claim a census of every appearance in every spin-off. Not D: his principal episode is covered completely with event identities kept.

Decisive controls are located: he will not withdraw from the Wiz dispute even for Vanir (C3 P441); Darkness's noble identity does not visibly constrain him; he threatens Small before crediting a reason for restraint; his claimed lie-sensing theory (C4 P382-384) fails to identify Aqua or the speakers' referents; the explicit job correction defeats a sincere-suitor reading; his lich upgrade immediately creates an adverse match-up; MAIN15 P788 says Axel was already targeted, blocking a sole-cause claim; and MAIN17 U011 P84 compares, not identifies, the white-winged gatekeeper. Not A: the controls come from one episode. Not C: they are specific and decisive.

Claims carry chapter and paragraph locators; the information states of each participant are ordered (Wiz's reported approach versus Kazuma's lip-read observation versus his paraphrases; Duke's hostile reports about Kazuma before he integrates them); the post-defeat romance is not projected backward; and later attributed outcomes are ordered and not backdated. Not A: the scope is one episode with bounded spin-off context. Not C: the ordering and anti-backdating controls are explicit.

conditions: Illustrative lines only, never presented as quotation, in a sampled function: grand self-introduction or challenge, contempt toward a perceived weak interferer, strained clarification under misunderstanding, a cautious polite request to Vanir, or a survival appeal after defeat.
Choose register by recipient rank and goal; no single arrogant register through every danger and no mandatory catchphrase.
No line expressing an original romantic goal toward Wiz before the post-defeat appeal, and no heard delivery claims.
scenario_readiness.note: The items constrain recipient-dependent register and speech function enough for short illustrative lines in sampled situations, not Japanese line imitation.

conditions: Only DK-R01: before predicting, fix his active aim, what he knows of the interlocutor's power, the affiliation he credits, whether Vanir is present, the actual interference and the material danger.

A weak interferer without a credited connection: intimidation or contempt is plausible, though a warning, refusal or dismissal may serve; with a credited Vanir connection, a qualified threat and room for dismissal or negotiation (moderate locally).
Vanir himself: caution and deferential address while still asserting that his own challenge proceeds; affiliation never transfers control of his central goal.

Abstain on an unconnected weak demon, a credible connection without an immediate threat, a false claimed patron, an explicit order to abandon his project and unfamiliar institutions, which the items leave open.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Pre-defeat MAIN13 and the DUST05 Small encounter, before the graveyard defeat and lich conversion; no post-defeat or later-reported state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: A perceived weak interferer (as Dust), an apparent supporter (as Kazuma), someone he credits as connected to Vanir (as Small), Vanir himself, or Wiz as the officeholder he challenges; anyone else only as a separate, lower-confidence case.
setting_constraints: Canonical mode: Axel tavern and challenge settings with his demonstrated fire and holy spells, knife, information gathering and the depicted ritual; no invincibility and no unestablished patron network.
Mundane transfer requires an explicit new institution, stated available means and a weaker analogy for rank; it supplies no supernatural aura, magic or new professional skill.
No anime adaptation or unreceived spin-off material.

scenario_readiness.note: A narrow bounded extrapolation under DK-R01 only; motive ordering, costly revision and unfamiliar institutions are excluded.
A few tavern transactions and one rapport scene with Aqua are located, but no conditioned account of his ordinary social conduct exists and the items state no routine or private life.
His justifications are interested testimony, no weighing between options is reported, and the single costly ideological revision happens under defeat and is deliberately not generalized.

No original romantic goal is established: the courtship reading is Wiz's and Kazuma's misunderstanding, corrected by his explicit job demand, and his final romantic appeal is a survival maneuver under imminent destruction.

conditions: Only the source-world military-office challenge: pursuit of the office through a demonstration of force, information gathering and reporting to the army, with his demonstrated spells and the depicted ritual.
His intelligence acquisition does not make his inferences sound (the courtship and Aqua-identity gaps), and his report is not the sole origin of the campaign against Axel.
No exact level, unlimited reserve, immunity or competence outside the demonstrated domains.
scenario_readiness.note: His military-office ambition is located; general professional competence and mundane institutions are not.

known_limits.statement: The model earns one provisional rule about interpersonal treatment under standing and affiliation; the lich conversion and improvised romance are bounded source explanations, not generators.

Ordinary caution around a much stronger figure, fear of retaliation, face-saving and generic patronage can generate much of the behavior DK-R01 explains; one specific connection may carry the whole effect.
The ordering among military standing, mastery, independence from divine service and survival is unknown.
Affiliation changes his treatment of a person but not his central challenge: he will not withdraw from the Wiz dispute even for Vanir.
His final romantic appeal is a new survival maneuver under imminent destruction and is never projected backward as the purpose of his arrival.
The later white-winged gatekeeper is a different figure; MAIN17 U011 P84 compares the two.

His lie-sensing theory is a claimed diagnostic that fails, his unpaid-wages grievance is testimony, and his report is not the sole cause of Axel's targeting; his later death is a retrospective narrator report.
No scenario input or original first response has been serialized; any later exercise is a dependent same-author diagnostic, and no accuracy or readiness is claimed.

His response to an unconnected weak demon, a credible connection without an immediate threat, a false claimed patron, an explicit order to abandon his project or an unfamiliar mundane institution is not established.
The cohort evidence index, native provenance and rule inventory are not curated on this subject, so their contents were not read as evidence.
